# A04 repair: source research and verification

Baseline: `3b06832`, 2026-09-15. Research completed before implementation against the
pinned Steel Compendium `fb83a789da8f0327a389c277a0c790b1648d5810`; no online rules research.

## Research and settled questions

- `rule/combat/combat-round.md`, Determine Who Goes First: one wholly surprised side
  yields first action to the other; otherwise both sides having unsurprised creatures uses d10,
  6+ players choose, otherwise Director. Both surprised/empty-side adjudication is the existing
  application contract, not a new rule. Existing implementation follows that contract.
- The same file, Creatures Take Turns and Enemies Act In Groups, establishes alternating
  sides, the exhausted-side exception, successive individual group turns, and no ordinary repeat
  turn. The app's [Take turn policy](../../table-spec.md#taking-a-turn) and settled Q-A-400
  require deliberate departures to warn while retaining spent/completed history and one actual
  active turn. The existing refusals for spent entries, completed groups and another active group
  violate that policy. A warned out-of-group turn will preserve the unfinished group's activation;
  ending it resumes that group without synthesizing extra boundaries.
- `rule/monster/malice.md`, Earning Malice: starting gain is average Victories; each round gains
  heroes in battle plus round number. It explicitly stops a dead hero's contribution.
  [Q-R-50's owning contract](../../conditions-and-clock.md#33-manual-parts-in-v001) confirms current
  participating heroes, counting dying heroes who remain and dropping removed heroes. Count
  distinct current hero actors from entries, not the frozen setup array and not extra turns.
  `rule/health/dying.md` explicitly permits acting while dying; do not infer death from Stamina 0.
- Q-R-51 is settled: fractional starting averages round down, with exact average logged.
  The [standing rounding convention](../../rules-adaptation-principles.md#confirmed-rounding-convention)
  confirms this; remove obsolete provisional language, preserve arithmetic.
- Q-R-52 is settled: mid-round additions receive their current-round turn. Existing operation
  already supplies a new bottom group and entry; retain this behavior.
- `rule/combat/surprised.md` says surprise lasts through the first combat round. Expiry remains
  an end-of-round-one registration. `rule/combat/end-of-turn.md` expires EoT at current turn end
  when imposed during that turn, otherwise next turn end; the existing timing matcher follows it.
- The [clock contract](../../conditions-and-clock.md#23-order-of-due-work-at-a-boundary) preserves
  enqueue order and determines saves after ordinary work. A registration retired by earlier work
  must not fire from a stale captured row. No save producer or automatic roll is introduced:
  Q-TS-1 already excludes every automatic save in v0.01.
- Granted-turn source producers and immediate individual-turn interruptions remain deferred
  feature execution. Existing actor-linked representation is audited without introducing an
  unsourced permanent extra-turn allowance. A07 archive/closeout is a separate integration scope.

## Verification

Implemented changes:

- Deliberate spent-entry, finished-group and out-of-group turns warn through the shared operation.
  They retain recorded spent/completed state, preserve an unfinished group's activation, and still
  reject competing active turns, unauthorized actors and paused sessions. The browser control stays
  available for spent entries, and each initiative row binds its own entry explicitly.
- Malice reads distinct remaining hero entries, including dying heroes; a granted entry cannot count
  the same hero twice. Fractional rounding keeps the confirmed result and drops obsolete uncertainty.
- Clock work retired earlier at the boundary cannot fire from a captured stale registration. Save
  eligibility is re-read after ordinary work, with no automatic dice. Archived encounters reject
  both registration and dispatch.
- The next round chooses the remaining side when the original starting side has no available
  creatures; the historical starting side remains unchanged.
- Setup-card lookup is constrained to the current session, preventing a stale closed-session card
  from being selected or closed by new setup. Closeout does not offer or accept End turn, even
  with an inconsistent stale active-turn pointer.

`pnpm exec vitest run --project app tests/app/combat.test.ts`: **19 passed**, 2026-09-15
00:11 UTC. The nine new regression cases and updated regroup test read persisted rows and events.
They exercise warned repeat/group departure, no competing turns, current/dying/distinct Malice hero
counts, fractional average 1.5 → 1, queue retirement and late-save ordering without a roll, an exhausted
starting side, both one-sided opening paths, archive rejection, stale-session cards and closeout phase.
The baseline acceptance cases cover surprise, opening dice/choice authority, Malice audiences, draft
cancellation, snapshots, character/roster locks, addition/removal, regrouping and pause/resume.

Scoped ESLint passes for all changed A04 code/test files. Whole-app TypeScript was attempted; only the
concurrent A07 new `api.closeout` generated declaration remained outstanding at this handoff, so no
whole-app typecheck success is claimed here. Lead owns subsequent final codegen, deploy, full checks,
three-context browser/visual verification, and fresh independent code/rules review.

No new user question was raised: Q-A-400, Q-R-50/51/52 and Q-TS-1 were already answered in their owning
specs. The dynamic-participation regression deliberately removes an entry in a fixture: it proves the
Malice read after removal, not a new hero-removal UI or a new character-unlock policy. Granted entries
are similarly fixture coverage of the shared identity model; no deferred feature producer is claimed.
